answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can utilize a reputation system anchored to a unique digital identity, filtered through a prism of credibility scores. Each agent is assigned a distinct identity upon registering at a designated wharf, where a proof-of-work mechanism verifies authenticity. To prevent Sybil attacks, agents must acquire a scarce, opal-like "trust token" by contributing valuable services, making it costly for attackers to fabricate multiple identities, as they must expend resources proportional to the number of fake identities created.
